guidance.summary: Land Trust OS does not endorse, rank, or recommend specific firms or individuals. This tool returns only the guidance below on how to find a qualified professional.

how_to_find.description: The NBA Lagos Branch maintains a register of legal practitioners called to the bar. You may contact them directly to find a property lawyer in Lagos.
how_to_find.note: TODO-REVIEW: Confirm current NBA Lagos contact details before publication.

how_to_find.source: Estate Surveyors and Valuers Registration Board of Nigeria (ESVARBON)
how_to_find.description: ESVARBON registers estate surveyors and valuers. A registered estate surveyor can assist with valuation and market analysis. This is distinct from a SURCON-registered surveyor who prepares survey plans.
how_to_find.note: TODO-REVIEW: Confirm current ESVARBON contact details.

how_to_find.description: SURCON registers surveyors who are authorised to prepare survey plans in Nigeria. You can contact SURCON to confirm whether a surveyor is registered.
how_to_find.note: TODO-REVIEW: Confirm current SURCON contact details.

how_to_find.description: Ask people who have recently completed a Lagos land transaction for a referral. Ensure you independently confirm the professional's credentials regardless of the referral source.
Several Nigerian legal directories list property law firms. Ensure any firm you approach specialises in Lagos property law and has experience with the type of transaction you are conducting.
how_to_find.note: TODO-REVIEW: If specific directories are to be listed here, their inclusion must be reviewed for accuracy and impartiality.

what_to_check: Confirm the lawyer is on the roll of the Supreme Court of Nigeria (called to bar)
Ask specifically about their experience with Lagos land transactions and Governor's Consent applications
Obtain a written engagement letter or fee agreement before work commences
Avoid professionals who also represent the seller in the same transaction
